attributes.nuance_translation: A word which may be used with either verbs or nouns, to express a variety of non-specific actions or things.

attributes.body:
とか is a word that belongs to a unique family of particles in Japanese called listing particles. As the name suggests, these particles are used for listing groups of items that share similarities. とか can be used after verbs, or nouns, to express 'among other things, (A)'.

When multiple things are listed, the last item in the list can (and often does) have とか omitted.

Caution

とか is used to list items in a non-exhaustive way. What this means is that the listener will assume that there are other items in the list, apart from what is stated directly. The speaker is just providing a few examples of a (potentially much larger) category.

Fun Fact

As we have seen, とか may be used with verb phrases. This is in contrast to や, a similar grammar point that can only be used for listing nouns.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: The Vague Listing 「や」 and 「とか」 particles

attributes.body: なんか・なんて and とか～とか both give examples, but differ in tone and usage. なんか・なんて usually follows a single noun to imply 'things like (A)', often with a dismissive or belittling nuance. とか～とか is used after each item in a list and simply means 'things like (A), (B), and so forth' without any negative implication.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: While both やら～やら and とか～とか list examples, they differ in nuance. やら～やら often has an uncertain tone or a presents contradictory possibilities, e.g. 行くのやら行かないのやら ('whether he's going or not'). とか is more neutral and casual, simply listing examples without a strong nuance of uncertainty.

first_relatable.title: やら～やら
first_relatable.meaning: Whether or, Things like, And … so on

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: Both たり～たりする and とか～とか are used to give examples of actions, similar to the English '(doing) things like A and B.' The key difference is how they attach to words. たり is made by adding り to the た (past tense) of a verb, while とか follows the dictionary form. Also, とか can follow nouns directly, while たり requires だ to become だったり.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: たとえば and とか～とか both introduce examples, but differ in usage. たとえば comes at the start of a sentence or clause, like 'for example'. In contrast, とか～とか is used to list multiple items and follows each noun. Because they differ in function, they can be used together in the same sentence, e.g. たとえば本とか雑誌とか ('For example, things like books, magazines, and so forth.').

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: など and とか～とか both list examples, but differ in nuance and structure. など usually follows a single noun or ends a list, implying the items are representative, like '(A) and so on' or 'things like (A).' とか～とか follows each noun and emphasizes specific, individual examples, like '(A) and (B), for example'.

first_relatable.title: など
first_relatable.meaning: Such as, Things like, Etc., And so on

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: し～し and とか～とか both list things, but with a different nuance. し～し lists reasons or causes, like 'because of things like (A) and (B)'. とか～とか simply lists items without implying they are a cause for something else, i.e. 'things like (A), (B), and so forth'. Also, とか～とか is very casual, while し～し will be found in both speech and writing.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: While both ～なり～なり and とか～とか present examples, they differ in formality and nuance. ～なり～なり is more formal and presents possible choices without preference. とか～とか is casual and used in everyday speech to mean 'things like (A) and (B),' often implying there are other possible examples.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: といった and とか～とか both give examples, but differ in structure and nuance. といった is used in the form AといったB to mean '(B) such as (A)', e.g. サッカーといったスポーツ ('sports such as soccer'). とか～とか follows each noun to list examples, e.g. サッカーとか野球とか ('things like soccer and baseball').

first_relatable.title: といった
first_relatable.meaning: Such as, Like, So much as

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: Both や and とか～とか are used to list items non-exhaustively, implying that other, unmentioned items are also included. や is more common in writing or formal speech, while とか is more colloquial. や must follow nouns, while とか can also be used with actions or events involving verbs. Additionally, とか can follow each item in the list, whereas や is not used after the final item.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as
